summary: This bill establishes a pilot program for one-stop paratransit services, mandates regulations for accessible pedestrian facilities, improves the process for reporting accessibility complaints, and creates a pilot program to collect and provide accessibility data for transportation planning, all to enhance transportation access for individuals with disabilities.

scores.thoughts: This bill authorizes $75,000,000 for each of fiscal years 2025 through 2029 to carry out the one-stop paratransit pilot program, which represents a direct increase in government spending for this specific initiative. It also mandates the Secretary of Transportation to carry out an accessibility data pilot program using existing administrative funds, which could lead to some reallocation or increased utilization of those funds.

The bill authorizes $75 million annually for FY2025–2029 (total $375 million) to fund the one-stop paratransit pilot program, with no offsetting revenue or cuts specified. This new discretionary spending has only minor, tangential implications for the deficit because the legislation's core purpose is expanding disability-accessible transportation rather than fiscal policy.
